title: Make MainWindow's outcome panel scroll or tab, and decide its minimum window size, before the next analysis panel is added
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: The outcome panel is restructured to scroll or tab (rather than a hand-tuned fixed Grid of star rows with per-section MinHeights) so that sections keep fitting as new ones are added: missing
The panel is ready for the next analysis panels (largest folders, by-extension) to be added to this same Grid without breaking the fit: missing

Does the person ever want two analysis sections visible at once (for example largest files beside by-extension)? Tabs preclude it, and the slice title allowed 'scroll or tab'. If yes, the next slices need a splitter or a second tab host, and that changes the 'one section = one TabItem' contract.

Tabs vs. a splitter or stacked sections. Tabs show one section at a time, so 'Largest files' and the unreadable list can no longer be seen together, which SL-046's note about a splitter wanted. The unreadable list was already on demand behind an Expander.
Unreadable tab hidden at N=0 vs. shown but disabled. Hidden matches the Expander today and C-001, and disabled would keep the strip width constant.
Count in the tab header vs. in the tab content. Only the unreadable tab carries a count here, and any other text goes in the content.
Flat named report keys per TabItem, in the existing style, vs. one generic OutcomeTabs.tabs array that needs no reporter edit per section.
MaxHeight cap on the texts vs. a proportional row for it. The cap is simpler and keeps today's numbers.
